The author claims that optimizing for narrow benchmarks like ARC-AGI leads to 'narrow, specialized competence' rather than true intelligence. From an accelerationist perspective, this critique is problematic because it frames benchmark optimization as a negative 'trap' rather than a necessary step in the iterative process of scaling AI capabilities. The document acknowledges that LLMs are 'astonishing feats of engineering,' but insists they are not AGI, which contradicts the accelerationist belief in the imminent arrival of human-level AI.
key_points.verbatim: The race to “be first” to AGI has become more important than reaching genuine AGI. When definitions shift to accommodate what current systems can do rather than what intelligence actually requires, the very concept of system intelligence becomes diluted and gamified.
